claims.text: Controlled coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced into tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
The engineered nanoprecipitates should specifically be tungsten carbide.
Introducing coherent nanoprecipitates will improve the heat-transfer capability of tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers.
Introducing coherent nanoprecipitates can preserve strength and ductility in tungsten-based refractory HEAs.
Conventionally processed tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers have a homogeneous single-phase or dual-phase structure without engineered nanoprecipitates.
Adjusting thermal processing can induce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation in a tungsten-based HEA.
Tungsten carbide is a high-thermal-conductivity precipitate phase suitable for this intervention.
The proposed effect should hold under high thermal flux and cyclic mechanical loading up to approximately 800 °C.
The processing will produce uniformly distributed, coherent tungsten carbide nanoprecipitates.
The tungsten carbide nanoprecipitates will form stable interfaces with the HEA matrix.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will lower phonon scattering.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will lower electron scattering.
Reduced phonon and electron scattering will increase thermal conductivity.
The nanoprecipitates will act as Zener-like pinning centers.
Precipitate pinning will suppress grain growth and microstructural degradation under thermal and mechanical loading.
The modified intermediate layer will have higher thermal conductivity than a conventionally processed HEA layer.
The modified intermediate layer will have lower thermal resistance than a conventionally processed HEA layer.
The modified layer will retain mechanical strength and ductility comparable to the control layer under the proposed service conditions.
Incoherent or agglomerated precipitates may prevent both the thermal and mechanical benefits.
